interpretation: The pooled habitat-continuity association weakens under equal-node within-transect comparison: the point estimate remains positive and 11/15 informative nodes are positive, but the frozen 95% interval slightly overlaps zero. Persistent transect-level habitat quality is therefore a plausible contributor to the pooled return association, with microsite continuity remaining suggestive rather than formally supported.
next_hypothesis: Test a pre-loss local legacy hypothesis: whether exact meter marks with longer pre-loss Thalassia occupancy history are more likely to re-record Thalassia after a one-year loss, beyond loss-year vegetation state and stable transect identity.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc reference-saturation audit of an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Do not claim a robust within-transect facilitation or refuge effect; the frozen equal-node CI overlaps zero.
The positive direction in 11/15 nodes is descriptive and does not replace the failed support rule.
Persistent node-level habitat quality, residual rhizomes, microsite conditions, and observation persistence remain plausible contributors.
Return remains recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not demographic recolonization.
